feast.note: The Greek calendar keeps the same four apostles on its own 30 October and the Romanian keeps this one on 10 noiembrie; this is the Russian calendar's own day and not a second day on one calendar. His name page lists «4 января (70 ап.)», the synaxis of the Seventy, and «30 октября»; one row per church is the schema, so the synaxis is recorded here and he does not render on it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 30 октября ст. ст. — «Апп. от 70-ти Тертия , Марка , Иуста и Артемы (I).»
source.note: The line is the second of the day. The day carries one typikon sign only, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком», so no rank is recorded.

attestations.note: The Russian prints the same four names as the Greek line this folder's Greek row quotes, and its one life for the four adds to his notice a people and a death: that he turned many of the pagans of Iconium to Christ, and that he ended his life there as a martyr. The see and the predecessor are the Greek page's as well. The calendar's index of lives under his name serves a third page besides the four's and his own, headed «Священномученик Терентий, епископ Иконийский», whose «Дни памяти» include this day and the Romanian's 10 November and which has that man killed by a sharpened stake; the corpus keeps no folder of that name and see, nothing here folds the two names, and the folder takes only what the four's own life says.

saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 30ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιοι Τέρτιος, Μάρκος, Ιούστος και Αρτεμάς οι Απόστολοι από τους Εβδομήκοντα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 30 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους». The folder's Romanian row keeps him on 10 November, a different day, and that row is not touched: this is the Greek calendar's own day for the same man, and he is identified not by his name but by what the page says of him — second bishop of Iconium after Sosipater, and the man who wrote down Saint Paul's letter to the Romans, as he says himself at Romans 16.22. The entry enumerates four apostles of the Seventy; two of them, Artemas of Lystra and Justus of Eleutheropolis, are new folders of this batch, and the fourth, Mark, is reported and not drafted because the corpus's Mark of Apollonias already carries a venerated Greek row on 16 June. No year, so the folder's dateless state is unchanged. No hymn on this page. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 12.11.2025 (30. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. ап. Клеопа, Терције, Марко, Јуст и Артем.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, second of the five apostles it enumerates. THE HEADING ENUMERATES FIVE APOSTLES — «Клеопа, Терције, Марко, Јуст и Артем» — so the brief’s enumeration ruling makes it one folder per named member, and all five rows quote the whole heading. FOUR of the five take a row here. THE FIFTH, Марко, TAKES NOTHING: `mark-of-byblos` already carries a venerated serbian row out of this same book’s Julian 27 September, where it identifies him in the same words this entry does, and section 1 makes a saint already venerated on another day report-only. The reading is in the commit message. ONE `types` ROW ADDED, READ AND NOT ASSUMED: `martyr`, off «скончао мученички као епископ Иконијски» — he ended in martyrdom as bishop of Iconium. The folder held `apostle` alone and the `office` «Bishop of Iconium», which this sentence confirms. `hieromartyr` WAS REFUSED: the book states the martyrdom and the bishopric in one clause but does not use the compound rank word, and composing a third grade out of two facts a book states separately is my arithmetic and not its reading — the same refusal made for `stephen-the-sabaite`’s missing see on the Julian 28 October. `dates` UNTOUCHED: the folder holds `death` 1 to 100, «1st century», off the Russian calendar’s «(I)» for the day’s apostles, and this entry gives no year at all. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND BOTH ARE NEW TO THIS FOLDER. HE WROTE PAUL’S EPISTLE TO THE ROMANS, with the chapter and verse printed — Рим. 16, 22 — which is the Tertius who says «I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, greet you in the Lord». AND HE WAS BISHOP OF ICONIUM AFTER THE APOSTLE SOSIPATER, with the book’s own cross-reference to its 10 November entry. That succession is why this folder already relates `sosipater-of-iconium`, both ways, so no `related` row is owed — and the row was written off another source, which this book now independently grounds. No `locations`: Iconium is named and is already in the `office`. THE FORM IS FREE: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Терције», which is worth noting because the corpus keeps several Terences and one of them took the Serbian «Теренције» two days ago — a different string, a different key, no collision. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day’s verse is Bishop Nikolai’s own and is about king Milutin. **A SECOND DAY OF THIS SAME BOOK, added 7 October 2026 by the reader of the Julian 10 November.** That day’s first entry is „Св. апостоли Олимп, Ераст, Кварт, Родион, Сосипатер и Терције.“, an enumerated heading of six in which this man is named «Терције», and its body then prints the cross-reference itself — «Последња тројица спомињу се још и на другом месту, и то: Родион 8. априла, Сосипатер 28. априла, а Терције 30. октобра», the last three are commemorated in another place as well. So the Prologue keeps him on the Julian 10 November too, which it serves at the civil 23.11.2025, read 7 October 2026. One attestation row per church is the schema, so the second day is recorded here and THIS ROW IS OTHERWISE UNCHANGED — same day, same month, same source, same text; he renders on the day above and not on 10 November. What that entry adds to him beyond the day is in the commit message for the Serbian 10 November and not in this folder: it gives each of the six a see or a death in one clause.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 30 октября ст. ст. closes the four apostles with «(I)», the first century, and its life for them gives no year. The folder held no `dates` before this: neither doxologia.ro nor saint.gr dated him at all.
